questions.question: What does BoatAttack do, and who runs it?
questions.answer: BoatAttack is a Unity Universal RP demonstration and learning/testing project: a vertical slice of a boat racing game with boats and an island. Developers open it in Unity; a player build runs the demo.
requiredFacts: Unity Universal RP testing and learning demo
Opened in Unity or built as a player

evidence.excerpt:
# Boat Attack
###### Demo Project using the Universal RP from Unity3D

[![Click for Youtube Video](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/Verasl/BoatAttack/release/2019.3/Assets/Textures/UI/welcome-title.png)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PTNdhnqbhzSWUCfAinIefP5cfr6Dezuw/view)

This Unity project has been created to aid the testing and development of Universal RP. The project is a small vertical slice of a boat racing game, complete with race-able boats and island environment.

Feel free to post any issues, but know this is a 'as is' repo, it's meant more for discovery of how some of the Universal RP features work and a learning resource for some tricks.

**Project Features**:
  * Uses Universal RP from Unity
  * Mobile optimized, low poly, LODs, no compute
  * C# Jobs buoyancy system
  * Cinemachine camera setups
  * Shader Graph usage
  * Post-processing v3 with Volume blending
  * Addressables asset management package
  * Custom Universal RP rendering for planar reflections via [SRP callbacks](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rendering.RenderPipelineManager.html)
  * Custom SciptableRenderPass usage for WaterFX and Caustics
  * Gerstner based water system in local package(WIP)
  * Much more..

#### Load the project:
Once you have the project files locally you can load the project, ideally in the Unity version that is noted in the `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` for the best experience.
Upon loading the project will display a small welcome screen with some buttons to load starting scenes.

Scenes worth noting:
 - `scenes/main_menu.unity` - Starting menu scene if you want to have a full play-through of the demo.
 - `scenes/demo_island.unity` - Setup to play in the editor and go straight into an AI based race.
 - `scenes/_levels/level_Island.unity` - The scene loaded when entering from the main menu.
 - `scenes/Testing/***.unity` - Assorted test scenes, these are in need of updating and come as is.

#### Build the project:
One thing to make sure you do before building is make sure to build the addressable assets, this can be done via the addressables window, for more information please checkout the addressables [package documentation](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.addressables@latest).
Once the addressable assets are built you can continue to build a player as usual.

One thing to mention is not all controls and platforms have been tested, especially for the menu work. if you want to just see the project running on a device you can add the `scenes/demo_island.unity` scene to the build list and disable/remove the others.

questions.question: Name the principal BoatAttack components and their responsibilities.
questions.answer: Boat gameplay scripts bind human or AI controllers to an Engine; the embedded WaterSystem package supplies URP water; scenes provide menu, island race and level entry; Cinemachine, Addressables and rendering features support cameras, assets and presentation.
requiredFacts: Menu and island scenes organize play
Cinemachine and Addressables provide camera and asset support

questions.question: Which languages, framework and package boundaries organize BoatAttack?
questions.answer: Gameplay is C# MonoBehaviour code in Assets/Scripts, run by Unity with Universal RP and the Input System. Packages/manifest.json declares package dependencies. Packages/com.verasl.water-system is a local package with its own package.json and WaterSystem runtime assembly definition. Shader Graph is also a documented rendering feature.
requiredFacts: Universal RP and Input System manifest dependencies
Embedded com.verasl.water-system package and WaterSystem asmdef

questions.question: Where does the selected human-controlled boat use begin?
questions.answer: The documented full-demo entry is the main_menu scene. For the selected gameplay slice, Boat.Setup calls SetupController, which selects HumanController when isHuman is true and attaches the component. Unity invokes HumanController.Awake/OnEnable/FixedUpdate; these lifecycle callbacks are engine dispatch, not a repository main function.
requiredFacts: Unity lifecycle is an external dispatch boundary

questions.question: Where is X, water-gated throttle acceleration, implemented?
questions.answer: Assets/Scripts/Boat/Engine.cs, Engine.Accelerate: when _yHeight > -0.1f it clamps modifier to [0,1], flattens and normalizes rigidbody forward, then applies horsePower-scaled acceleration and relative torque.
requiredFacts: Applies forward force and relative torque

questions.question: Which internal components does A, HumanController, directly use, and what proves each direction?
questions.answer: HumanController constructs InputControls, calls Engine.Accelerate and Engine.Turn from FixedUpdate, calls Boat.ResetPosition for Reset, and DayNightController.SelectPreset for the debug time input. BaseController.OnEnable resolves the Boat component and its Engine. Input System and Unity lifecycle are external framework dependencies.

questions.question: For R, holding throttle on a human boat, give the supported path to acceleration and identify dispatch boundaries.
questions.answer: InputControls.BoatControls.Trottle.performed stores ReadValue<float>() in _throttle; canceled sets it to zero. Unity FixedUpdate calls engine.Accelerate(_throttle), whose water gate and clamp precede Rigidbody.AddForce and AddRelativeTorque. BaseController obtains engine from Boat. Input callbacks, fixed-step scheduling and physics integration are Unity boundaries; source does not prove a particular frame was executed.
requiredFacts: Input callbacks and physics are engine-dispatched

questions.question: If Y, Engine.Accelerate throttle semantics, changes, which direct consumers are evidenced?
questions.answer: HumanController.FixedUpdate passes _throttle; AiController passes 1f or 0.25f according to dot > 0. These direct calls prove both controllers consume the method. Changed movement, balance or race results would require runtime validation, not merely these dependencies.
requiredFacts: Behavioral race impact is not established by call evidence

questions.question: Which documented example exercises X, boat acceleration, and how does it enter the implementation?
questions.answer: README documents demo_island as a scene that goes straight into an AI race. The corresponding source path is Boat.SetupController selecting AiController for non-human boats, whose update logic calls Engine.Accelerate. This is a documented manual example and static connection, not an executed test or a claim that every scene reference was resolved.

questions.question: Where does Z, throttle input, enter and get transformed?
questions.answer: HumanController.Awake subscribes to the intentionally spelled Trottle action and reads a float into _throttle; cancel resets it. FixedUpdate passes it to Engine.Accelerate, where the water-depth gate and 0..1 clamp precede horsePower scaling and force application.
